messages.content: {"rule": "Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and a new passage of about 250 words in the text field.", "text": "The northern headland was farther than it looked from the lamp room, and by the time they reached it the moon had risen, thin and sharp as a fingernail paring. The wind came hard off the water, flattening the grass and pulling at the lantern flame until the girl cupped her hand around the glass to shelter it. Her father walked ahead with the shovel over his shoulder, counting paces under his breath the way he counted the turns of the clockwork that drove the lens. The map showed the cross set between a crooked hawthorn and a stone that looked, in the drawing, like a sleeping dog. They found the hawthorn first, bent almost double by a century of gales. The stone took longer. It was half buried in bracken, but when the lantern light fell across it, the girl laughed out loud, because it truly did look like a dog curled with its nose tucked under its tail. Her father began to dig. The soil was thin and full of roots, and twice the shovel rang against rock. The girl held the lantern steady and watched his breath smoke in the cold air. At last the blade struck something that was not stone. It was a tin box, rusted nearly through, no bigger than a loaf of bread. Inside, wrapped in oilcloth, lay a brass key and a photograph of a woman standing on the lighthouse gallery, one hand raised as if to wave. Her father stared at it for a long moment. Then, very softly, he said his mother's name."}
